And I will then put my questions, which means that if we include tomorrow, that would amount to three hours, and on next Monday another three and a half hours to four hours. This means that you have approximately five or six hours. Can you finish in that time?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: A small question. You have referred twice, once just now to a "classeur," to a binder "Mostar-93." We have one binder which is inscribed "Mostar-92." Now, is this perhaps wrongly inscribed or will we get another binder?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you will not get a binder. You will get two documents in relation to Mostar, the snipers and the Old Bridge, not in the form of a binder. It's just my way of referring to it, "Mostar-93," but you won't be getting that. You will be getting a single new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have understood you correctly, Ms. Pinter, we will have to review all of these documents and additional documents on Mostar-93; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I have just been informed by our case manager that we have not yet handed over the binder that I mentioned, documents to be explained. These are all exhibits and documents that we believe the general should comment on, on the circumstances under which these documents were produced, how they came about and why. These documents are exhibits. We've sifted through these documents, and there aren't many that still remain. We believe that we will be able to complete this by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. We're talking about procedural matters. I have two minutes to have something explained. The interpretation that I have now received is Mr. President, Judge Antonetti, has the intention of asking his questions immediately after the close of the examination-in-chief. I just wanted to check whether that was, in fact, the case, since the Prlic Defence is the first up for cross-examination, just in order to allow us to better plan our own time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Listen. I believe it is better if I put my question straight after, and the Prlic Defence can then put its questions. Otherwise -- well, I'll think about it, and I'll let you know tomorrow. I'll tell you what my position is. But if the other accused are to purposefully cross-examine Mr. Praljak, I believe it would be better for you to know beforehand what my questions will be and what Mr. Praljak's answers will be, rather than intervening or taking the floor and then I put follow-up questions, questions which you will not be able to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, it was not my intention at all to challenge your decision. All I was seeking was a clarification, no more than that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to clarify this. I will, for instance, address the issue of the criminal enterprise with Mr. Praljak. I will put questions to him on the kind of relationship he had with Mr. Prlic. So as far as I'm concerned, I think it's better if he answers, and then you can put your questions afterwards. And you can turn to him and say, When you answered, you said this and that, rather than if I put my questions and then you are in a bit of a conundrum.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I fully understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just in case you get to hear the opinion of the other Defence teams, on behalf of General Petkovic, we believe this to be an outstanding proposal, Your Honour, for you to ask your questions right after the chief. That will make it possible for us to focus our own cross-examination on questions that you will indicate as relevant in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to say that prior to your decision, there were discussions between the Defence teams, I even spoke to Mr. Stringer from the OTP about that, and that was precisely the proposal that we were going to make to you before the cross-examinations begin, precisely the decision that you took. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not just rising for the sake of saying something, anything, at all. But if I may be so bold, I think it might be a good idea for all of the remaining Judges to ask their questions right after the Presiding Judge, which would make the cross-examination much easier for all the remaining Defence teams. I mean if all the Judges were to ask their questions immediately after the in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be crystal clear - everything needs to be crystal clear - the Bench hasn't conferred on this matter. We don't know how we will proceed. I have said that I will put questions. My colleagues will do what they please. They will put questions or they won't. I want this to be very clear. A Judge that puts questions put questions under his own responsibility. He's taking the risk. I want this to be very clear. I believe I will put my questions when Mr. Praljak is finished. My colleagues may do likewise or may put questions after you. I don't know. That's for them to say. I personally will put questions to Mr. Praljak in line with the indictment. This is what I have indicated. I have said that I will first put to him questions pertaining to the Prosecution's pre-trial brief and documents; and in the second part, I will put questions based on the written submissions filed by Mr. Praljak, his initial pre-trial brief, and his more recent submissions, so that this is balanced out. My colleagues do what they feel they should do. This is their responsibility. I know that some Trial Chambers proceed differently. In other cases, a Judge is designated to put the questions. This is not the way I understand international justice. I feel that in the present case, the issues are so complex that we need to put questions. Since we have an accused who is prepared to take the stand as a witness, well, we should benefit from this. The other accused and Defence counsel can, during their cross-examination, review or visit other issues; for instance, the relationship he had with Mr. Petkovic. This will certainly be of interest to Ms. Alaburic, and this will depend on the answers provided by Mr. Praljak. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Stringer. Simply to be on the record, I would like to say that, of course, I am looking forward to the questions to be asked by Mr. President. On the other hand, myself, I do not wish to ask any other particular questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: As for me, I have, for reasons of principle, planned not to ask a systematic set of questions of the witness. But I, of course, may ask spontaneous questions whenever something comes up, as I have done it with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just for the record - and Ms. Tomasegovic has already indicated a conversation we had - the Prosecution position on this would be that all of the parties should have the opportunity to either do cross-examination or at least do follow-up questions after a Judge has presented his or her questions to the witness. And so it doesn't matter to us so much when that happens. So it seems to me, Mr. President, that the procedure that's envisioned, whereby the President will be asking his questions in advance of the cross-examination by any of the other parties is perfectly in line with that, in that all of the parties then would have an opportunity to cross-examine afterwards. So it seems perfectly sensible to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'd like to thank all and every one for having concluded that my proposal makes sense, which I did not doubt for a second. It's always very comforting to be supported in such a way. It's just about 7.00. As far as tomorrow is concerned, we will have only one break. We will have a break -- this is something I've discussed with my colleagues already. This first break will occur after the first series of questions. The break might be 20 or 30 minutes' long. Much will depend on the way things unfold tomorrow. We will resume and finish around 6.00. On Monday, we will finish, so you will have a lot of time. For your information, you've had one hour of extra time so far, so you have a lot of time left to finish on Monday. As I have said already, we will have a break for a few days, which means that everyone can get ready for the rest of the proceedings. It is now 7.00. Tomorrow, we will resume and address the issue of effective control, and I wish everyone a pleasant evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of June, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The Accused Prlic and Coric not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
